**Finding: MISSING** — no vendor insurance covenant (confidence 0.86)

**What I checked.** I searched the full document for insurance language and read every hit plus the planner's candidate analogues:

- **SOW 13.1(b)** — the only MSL insurance obligation: replacement-value cover for *consigned Products only*, with IBM as joint insured.
- **SOW 21.2 (Care)** — obliges *IBM* to insure its own tooling; MSL is only jointly insured "where possible." Runs the wrong direction for this rule.
- **Loan Agreement § 8** — IBM *relieves* MSL of risk of loss on Loaned Items (favourable to MSL, but no insurance).
- **§ 10.0** — premises terms deferred to a separate Lease of Premises Agreement not in this document.
- **§ 16.0 General (16.1–16.21)** — no insurance subsection anywhere.

**Why it fails the fallback.** The existing cover is purely first-party property insurance on inventory. There is no commercial general liability, no professional liability, no cyber/privacy and no workers' compensation cover, so the document does not reach even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). The exposure is real rather than theoretical: MSL occupies IBM premises under the lease, holds both IBM and IBM-customer consigned inventory (13.1(a)), and accesses IBM applications, networks and customer integration data under SOW 24.1 — the precise profile the rule targets. The absence of any liability cover for a vendor on our premises handling our customers' data sits in walk-away territory.

**Redline** (validated `ok:true`): a new **Section 16.22 Insurance** inserted at the end of the General section, at the preferred limits — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where MSL touches IBM or IBM-customer data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request, term plus one year.

Two drafting points worth flagging for the negotiation:

- I expressly preserved the 13.1(b) consigned-Products cover ("in addition to") so the new clause cannot be read as narrowing or superseding a protection we already hold.
- The comment offers the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) up front, since MSL's existing programme may already sit near that level and this is a low-severity rule not worth stalling on.

One item outside my scope to verify: the separate **Lease of Premises Agreement** may already carry premises-related liability and property cover. If it does, the CGL limb here may overlap and could be trimmed — worth confirming against that document before sending.
